requirement:
Habeas MUST document the user and project configuration locations, the common
file structure and schema version, and how to create and edit the files by hand.
Each configurable feature MUST document its fields, defaults, resolution rules,
and credential-source references, with complete, copyable examples identifying
all placeholders and the file to edit. Documentation MUST explain how to change
or remove optional settings and selections.

Configuration MUST NOT require a configuration-management command or generated
state beyond the documented files. Primary examples MUST use credential-source
references; examples explaining explicit credential fields MUST use clearly
identified placeholders, never real secrets.
rationale:
## Determination

The documentation and its referenced tests satisfy `requirements.configuration.documentation`.

## Obligations and coverage

The subject imposes these separate obligations: document (1) user locations, (2) project locations, (3) common structure, (4) schema version, (5) creation by hand, (6) editing by hand; document each feature's (7) fields, (8) defaults, (9) resolution rules, and (10) credential-source references; provide examples that are (11) complete, (12) copyable, (13) identify every placeholder, and (14) identify the file to edit; explain (15) changing optional settings, (16) removing optional settings, (17) changing selections, and (18) removing selections; require neither (19) configuration-management commands nor (20) additional generated configuration state; and ensure (21) primary examples use credential-source references and explicit-credential examples (22) identify placeholders clearly and (23) contain no real secrets.

- **Locations, structure, version, and manual maintenance (1–6, 19–20):** `md/reference.md#section[How%20it%20works]/section[Authoring%20evidence%20with%20a%20model]` gives Unix and Windows user paths, nearest-enclosing workspace scope, UTF-8 TOML, `version = 1`, permitted feature tables, and explicit instructions to create and edit the files with a text editor. It describes no management-command or generated-state prerequisite. `md/requirements/configuration.md#section[Configuration]/section[Common%20data%20structures]` supplies the common schema and minimal complete file. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[configuration_documentation_covers_locations_structure_editing_and_removal]` asserts the location, structure, version, and manual-maintenance statements; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[documented_configuration_examples_are_complete_valid_files]` parses the documented files directly.
- **Feature documentation (7–10):** The reference section documents authoring, evidence path policy, and coverage settings, including defaults, precedence, and AWS-profile/environment credential references. The common-data-structures section defines evidence and coverage fields. The linked `md/requirements/authoring.md#section[Authoring%20evidence]/section[Configuration]` provides the authoring structures and detailed field, default, serialization, and resolution rules. Its `section[Editing%20the%20file]` subsection supplies backend-specific editing instructions, including OpenAI. The phrase-coverage test above asserts defaults, selection precedence, and credential-source instructions. Remaining static field descriptions have no conditional execution or transformation requiring separate runtime tests.
- **Examples (11–14):** Complete TOML examples in those marked documentation sections name user `config.toml` or workspace `habeas.toml`, identify replacement values, and can be copied without reconstructing omitted configuration syntax. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[documented_configuration_examples_are_complete_valid_files]` parses the examples; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[documented_configuration_examples_name_the_file_to_edit]` checks their introductory file identification and parses them for the stated scope; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[documented_configuration_examples_identify_their_placeholders]` checks surrounding placeholder explanations.
- **Changing and removing settings and selections (15–18):** The reference and editing subsection explain editing defaults and project selections, deleting keys or tables, updating selections when deleting configurations, editing evidence arrays, and restoring defaults by removing optional settings. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[configuration_documentation_covers_locations_structure_editing_and_removal]` asserts both the general removal rule and concrete selection, endpoint, and concurrency instructions. The remaining explanatory prose is static, with no conditional or transformation of its own.
- **Credential examples (21–23):** Primary authenticated examples use `aws_profile` or `api_key_env`; unauthenticated local Ollama examples need no credential. The explicitly labeled literal-credential example in `md/requirements/authoring.md#section[Authoring%20evidence]/section[Configuration]/section[Editing%20the%20file]` uses uppercase placeholders and tells readers to replace them. The complete-file test restricts literal-credential examples to that chapter and verifies that their secret-field values contain only uppercase placeholder characters. The placeholder test checks their identification, and the phrase-coverage test checks credential-source examples. The inline OpenAI literal-key explanation likewise explicitly identifies `OPENAI_API_KEY_VALUE` as a replacement placeholder.

All cited tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. The documentation implementing these obligations is within the supplied `{impl}` sections or their linked schema material. No unmet obligation or acknowledged gap was found.
